entries.clue: Johnson on fatherhood: "It's a healthy option to some extent" (3-3)

annotation.definitionNote: The definition is a noun phrase; the answer is an adjective describing such an option.

indicatorNotes.to some extent: Something true only to some extent is partly true, so only part of the quoted text is used and the answer sits within it.

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of Johnson across 'on' into fatherhood

annotation.surface: A quote from Boris Johnson, father of many, praising parenthood as good for you.
annotation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make it look like Johnson is speaking about his many children; the answer straddles the join of his name and the next two words.
annotation.definitionFit: Skimmed milk and low-fat yoghurt are sold as the lighter, diet-friendly choice on supermarket shelves.

entries.clue: Access by bloke, upset showing ID (7)

annotation.definitionFit: Conference badges pinned to a lapel identify the wearer, so they serve as identification.

entries.clue: Patel's back covered by main Tory oddball – the usual state (9)

indicatorNotes.covered by: Something covered by another thing is wrapped inside it, so the L goes within the other letters.

annotation.surface: Priti Patel's position is propped up by a senior Tory eccentric, as ever.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Back' suggests support for Patel; it only means her final letter. The joke is that a Tory oddball should produce the opposite of the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: The noun names a condition matching the norm, how things ordinarily are when nothing odd happens.

entries.clue: Gulf close to being swamped by dope (5)

annotation.walkthrough: 'Close to' looks like an instruction to take a last letter, which would give G; here it simply means near. 'Dope' means a fool, not drugs.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a gulf can be a deep chasm or bottomless pit in the earth, not only a sea inlet.

entries.clue: As a Republican voter, was confrontational, angry-looking (3-5)

blocks.note: red is the Republicans' colour in the US
to face someone is to confront them

entries.clue: Hard to leave female-only Private Eye occasion (6)

HEN, as in a hen party for women only, loses its H
a tail is a private detective who follows people

annotation.surface: It is tough to walk out of a women-only Private Eye party.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Occasion' is a verb here, meaning to bring about; it looks like the noun completing 'Private Eye occasion'. A hen party or hen night is the British name for a bride's all-female party.
annotation.definitionFit: Both verbs mean to cause or necessarily bring about, as when a job involves travel.

entries.clue: Fail miserably to limit elected political party, money-wise (9)

indicatorNotes.miserably: Something done miserably is done badly, so FAIL comes out in a poor order.

annotation.surface: A failure to cap the finances of the ruling party.
annotation.walkthrough: The ANC is South Africa's governing party, a crossword regular for 'party'.
annotation.definitionFit: The suffix -wise means 'as regards', so money-wise means concerning cash and funds.

entries.clue: Conservative member's scramble (5)

blocks.note: an arm or leg is a member of the body

annotation.surface: A Tory MP's frantic rush, perhaps for a seat.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Member' suggests an MP; it is a body part. The 's stands for 'is'.
annotation.definitionFit: Scrambling means clambering upward using hands and feet over rocks, a kind of ascent.

entries.clue: Princess Di description of party executive leader given the Strobes treatment? (3-4)

entries.clue: Snag in advanced stage of erection? Don't lag behind (5,2)

a structure nearly finished is up

entries.clue: Pissed as Robin's band? (5)

blocks.note: British slang for drunk, not angry
the adjective attached to Robin Hood's outlaws

annotation.surface: Drunk like Robin Hood's outlaws.
annotation.walkthrough: In British slang 'pissed' means drunk, not annoyed; the answer is a milder word for being tipsy, and Robin Hood's band were the Merry Men.
annotation.definitionFit: Tipsy cheerfulness after a few drinks is one sense; the other is the epithet of Robin Hood's outlaw companions in Sherwood.

entries.clue: On the alert after a tense, temporary erection one has (9)

Gove is involved with right-wing Ukrainian sources? Deplorable (8)

blocks.clueFragment: Group formed by e.g. Johnson, Adams and Dorries

annotation.surface: Boris Johnson and his loyalists Nigel Adams and Nadine Dorries stirring up trouble, full of spite.

entries.clue: One needs Sunak to do a U-turn and break cover – that's clear (6)

annotation.definitionNote: The definition is a phrase describing something clear; the answer is the adjective.

indicatorNotes.break: To break cover is to burst through it, so the letters split the cover apart.

annotation.surface: Sunak must reverse a policy and come out of hiding, one insists.
annotation.walkthrough: Sunak stands for his job title, Prime Minister; 'break cover' is an idiom that here splits into instruction and piece.
annotation.definitionFit: Transparent water or prose, easy to see through or understand, is described with this literary adjective.

entries.clue: Persistent criminal tale fabricated about Ukraine's leader (9)

blocks.note: short for perpetrator, US police slang

annotation.walkthrough: 'Ukraine's leader' suggests Zelensky; it is only a first letter.

entries.clue: Cyclops, a nerd turned snake! (7)

entries.clue: Beastly thing – firm, yet badly crushing ball (6)

annotation.walkthrough: 'Beastly' sounds like nasty, but here it means simply belonging to the beasts.
annotation.definitionFit: A North American wild dog, the prairie wolf, is literally an animal, a beast.

entries.clue: Cabinet's no.1 bounder and prick (7)

blocks.note: something that bounds along, like a kangaroo

annotation.walkthrough: 'Bounder' is an old British word for a cad, but here it is literal: something that bounds.

entries.clue: Quite the gentleman, my Roger, in the sack (4-4)
